issues.legal_issue: A contractual minimum-production obligation coupled with a minimum-guaranteed-royalty term requires payment of the guaranteed royalty when production falls below the minimum and the requirement has not been relaxed.
material_facts: The agreement required the company to manufacture a minimum quantity of salt, in addition to the quantity needed for its own factory.
A separate term required minimum royalty based on the minimum quantity if the company failed to manufacture that quantity and the government did not relax the requirement.
Production fell below the stipulated minimum during the years in dispute, and the government had not relaxed the requirement.
issues.conclusion: The company was liable to pay the minimum guaranteed royalty for the years in which production fell below the contractual minimum.
issues.legal_principle: The agreement's royalty, minimum-production, and minimum-royalty terms must be read together. The minimum-royalty term is a special provision for shortfall years that supplements, rather than conflicts with, the ordinary royalty term; an interpretation that makes the minimum-production and minimum-royalty terms ineffective should be rejected. The Court relied on clauses 2 to 5 of the agreement and cited no earlier cases.

rule.if: civil_contract_appeal and contract_requires_minimum_output and contract_guarantees_minimum_payment_on_shortfall and production_fell_below_minimum and government_did_not_relax_requirement

predicates.civil_contract_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning the interpretation and enforcement of a contract.
predicates.contract_requires_minimum_output: The agreement requires one party to produce at least a specified minimum quantity.
predicates.contract_guarantees_minimum_payment_on_s: The agreement requires a minimum payment if the required output is not achieved.
predicates.production_fell_below_minimum: The producing party produced less than the contractual minimum.
predicates.government_did_not_relax_requirement: The government did not waive or reduce the minimum-production requirement.

issues.definition: When a civil contract appeal involves a minimum-output obligation, a guaranteed payment for shortfall, production below the minimum, and no relaxation of the requirement, the guaranteed payment is payable.

issues.legal_issue: Where a royalty term makes payment due on goods sold and delivered, royalty is calculated on the quantity sold and delivered rather than the total quantity manufactured.
material_facts: The agreement set royalty by reference to the quantity of salt sold and made payment due when delivery was given to a purchaser.
The dispute included whether royalty under that term could be calculated on the total quantity manufactured rather than the quantity sold and delivered.
issues.conclusion: Royalty under the ordinary royalty term was payable only on the quantity actually sold and delivered, not on the total quantity manufactured.
issues.legal_principle: The clear wording of clause 2 tied levy and collection of royalty to sale and delivery, so royalty under that clause applied only to the quantity actually sold and delivered. The Court relied on clause 2 of the agreement and cited no earlier cases.

predicates.civil_contract_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning the interpretation and enforcement of a contract.
predicates.royalty_clause_uses_sale_and_delivery_as: The agreement ties royalty payment to goods being sold and delivered to a purchaser.

issues.definition: When a civil contract appeal concerns a royalty term triggered by sale and delivery, royalty is calculated only on the goods sold and delivered.
